values: Google Maps screening determines who gets a call. Pilot checks determine who is ready to accept bookings.
Weights, cutoffs and the Tapovan–Muni Ki Reti starting area are initial operating choices. Review them after the first 10 calls.
Rental offer unclear after checking the listing and website.
Self-drive rentals confirmed as a secondary service or with a limited advertised range.
Self-drive scooter or motorcycle rentals are a core service with specific vehicle examples.
No dated rental-related signal in the last 180 days.
One dated signal in the last 90 days, or one or more in days 91–180.
At least two distinct rental-related signals in the last 90 days.
Repeated specific friction with response, punctuality or handover. Escalate serious concerns to Hold.
Evidence is thin or mixed, with no recurring serious issue.
At least two reviews specifically describe clear terms, good condition, or a smooth handover or return, with no repeated concern.
Pickup appears difficult or well outside the launch area.
Pickup is adjacent to the launch cluster or delivery into it is advertised; confirm timing and fees.
Clear pickup point in the launch cluster with practical access for customers.
No usable public contact or visit route.
Directory number, generic travel desk, or usable storefront address only.
Direct business phone or WhatsApp published by the shop.
Search shop name + locality. Check phone, address and storefront. Merge aliases with the same business and shared inventory.
Save the actual Maps listing URL and date checked. Search URLs in the tracker are starting points.
In scope for a credible local motorized self-drive rental. Hold if match or service is unclear. Exclude confirmed duplicates, closures or irrelevant listings.
Read up to 10 newest reviews; then scan low ratings for repeated issues within the past year. Check customer photos for context.
Record 1–2 specifics and dates. For activity, count dated rental reviews or clearly dated fleet updates. A few reviews can still be useful.
Hold for a concrete safety incident or repeated similar deposit, vehicle-condition or cancelled-pickup complaints. Verify with shop and a visit before clearing.
3. Score and make the call list
Enter all five scores. Leave blanks while research is unfinished. Points equal each grade divided by 2 times the weight.
Example: 2 rental, 2 activity, 1 handover, 2 pickup, 2 contact = 87.5. It earns a first call if in scope.
Call first ≥75. Call next 55 to below 75. Later <55. With 0 contact and ≥55, find a contact route. A scope Hold overrides any score.
Start with 10 leads in the launch cluster. Include two promising shops with fewer reviews if their rental offer is clear.
For tied scores, prioritize a missing vehicle category, then stronger recent evidence. Try to get two independent sources of the most requested vehicle type.
Choose by pickup coverage, vehicle mix and willingness to keep availability current. After 10 calls, compare demos booked and discovery findings by score.
Fleet authority and papers: verify who controls each pilot vehicle, and check documents and insurance for those vehicles.
Vehicle and pickup: inspect condition, helmets, and the handoff point. Availability: name the operator and have them record a walk-in and a blocked vehicle.
Agree rates, deposits, cancellations, payouts and escalation. Run a test booking through pickup and return. All five checks must pass.
Pilot 2–3 vehicles for 14 days. Log availability mismatches, merchant cancellations, handover issues and payout or deposit disputes.
Review actual completed pickups and returns. Track the owner’s response when availability changes or an issue comes up.
Expand after reliable handoffs on real bookings with no unresolved serious issue. With zero real bookings, extend the test before drawing conclusions.
Existing Rishikesh lead list supplies shop names, phone numbers and source URLs.
Google explains that local ranking reflects relevance, distance and prominence.
